proof.criterion: The install lock's wait holds its relation to the registration deadline at every configuration an operator can set, not only at the defaults.
proof.surface: TestTheInstallLockWaitIsABoundInProportionToTheRegistrationDeadline in packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox: four configurations — the daemon's own defaults read through config.LoadForValidation, a halved boot timeout, fewer intervals, and a deadline small enough that the floor bites — each asserting the wait positive, never more than its third of that deadline, and (where the deadline leaves room) two waits plus a second of install still inside it.
proof.observed: Green as it stands. Mutated to the raw third with no floor: `the wait at boot 800ms x 3 intervals is 0s, want a positive bound: a non-positive wait renders -w 0, which is -n, and restores the cold-entry race`. Mutated to a half instead of a third: `the wait at boot 2m0s x 3 intervals is 180s, more than its third of the 6m0s deadline`, with the halved-timeout and fewer-intervals cases failing beside it. Both restored, `ok … 0.021s`, and the file's checksum back to f491869a34cf9b7e.
proof.negativeControl: The test this replaces is the control: it asserted one constant against one deadline read from the defaults, so it would have passed the divisor mutation outright and could never see an operator's setting at all.

proof.criterion: The derived wait renders the same bound at the defaults, so the change makes the value unconditional rather than different.

proof.criterion: What a plugin install actually costs, so the next person sizing a timeout, a deadline or a retry budget against it reads a measurement instead of guessing.
proof.surface: `bun add --backend=copyfile --exact @sjawhar/pi-legion@10.14.0 @sjawhar/pi-envoy@10.12.0` in an issue pod of this cluster, into a fresh generation directory, with BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR empty and then warm.
proof.command: BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=<empty dir> /usr/local/bin/bun add --backend=copyfile --exact @sjawhar/pi-legion@10.14.0 @sjawhar/pi-envoy@10.12.0, timed, then repeated in a second directory against the cache it filled
proof.observed: cold exit=0 in 505 ms, leaving 3.4 MiB of cache and 3.3 MiB installed; warm exit=0 in 32 ms. So the remaining third of the deadline at the defaults, 120 s, covers the install it must cover by two orders of magnitude: the install side does not constrain this bound, the deadline side does. The order of magnitude is the claim — a pod on a cold node pulling from npm is slower.
proof.negativeControl: The warm run is the control for the cold one — same command, same pod, same pair, the cache the only difference — which is also what shows the cold fill, not the install out of it, is both the cost and the race.

proof.criterion: A derived wait that rounds down would restore the race silently, so the floor is a fence rather than tidiness.
proof.surface: /usr/bin/flock against a directory a holder process holds, in this pod.
proof.command: setsid flock -- cache sh -c 'sleep 10' & then flock -w 0 -- cache /bin/true ; flock -n -- cache /bin/true ; flock -w 1 -- cache /bin/true ; flock -w 3 -- cache /bin/true
proof.observed: -w 0: exit=1 after 0.00 s. -n: exit=1 after 0.00 s — byte for byte the same behaviour. -w 1: exit=1 after 1.00 s. -w 3: exit=1 after 3.00 s. So a wait that rounds to zero is no wait at all, and the floor is what stands between a small boot timeout and the unserialised cold fill arriving by arithmetic with every test still green.
proof.negativeControl: The bounded waits are the control for the zero ones: the same binary against the same held lock waits exactly as long as it is told, so the zero case is the flag's meaning rather than a broken rig.

proof.criterion: The lock rather than the retry is what removes the cold-fill failures — the question this implementer's own before/after could not answer.
proof.surface: The tester's control, recorded in .legion/INFRA-31/test.json and cited by name rather than re-derived: the rendered script with flock removed and the retry kept, run six-way cold in the tester's container.
proof.command: the tester's six-way cold run with the flock prefix stripped and `legion_install || legion_install` left in place
proof.observed: 2 of 6 failed both attempts on its first cold run, and its second passed only with `ENOENT: failed copying files from cache to destination` in two roles' logs, succeeding on the retry. With the lock in place the tester's post-fix cold runs were 6 of 6 exit 0 with ENOENT absent from every log.

packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/types.go, sandbox.go — Options.RegistrationIntervals beside BootTimeout, refused when not positive, carried onto the runtime.

packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins_test.go — the single-constant assertion replaced by the property over four configurations; the rendered-text pin builds its `-w <n>` from the same derivation over the options the spec configured.
rig_test.go, live_test.go and four internal/daemon tests — the new Options field, since configure now refuses it unset.
docs/kubernetes.md — the bound's sentence finishes its conditional: a third of the two settings' product, why a proportion rather than a number, and the one-second floor with its reason.
trickyParts: Reachability was one field short rather than zero: BootTimeout was already on sandbox.Options from cfg.WorkerBootTimeout, but the intervals reached only supervise.Timeouts, so the derivation needed RegistrationIntervals plumbed to the runtime that renders the script.

Deriving through runtime.RegistrationDeadline rather than re-multiplying means the wait follows the deadline if that ever stops being a plain product — the same discipline as naming a setting rather than a number, applied to a computation.

The floor dominates below a deadline of about three seconds, where two waits cannot fit. That is deliberate and stated in the test rather than excluded from it: being serialised and then retired by the deadline is no worse than racing, since an unserialised cold fill fails the launch anyway.

The wait is a parameter of the render because an operator's configuration determines it, which is what production shape is for — deliberately unlike a test's convenience, which this branch refused as a reason to widen a signature when the serialisation test instead substitutes its stub into the rendered text.
discoveredComplexity: A text assertion built from the value it pins cannot see that value change: the substring assertion over the rendered script constructed its expected `-w <n>` from the same constant it was pinning, so a mutation to zero left it green while the behavioural test and the bound's own test failed. Adding more such assertions would not have closed it.
